ground_truth.what_it_does: AI safety company that builds the Claude family of AI models, offered via API, consumer apps, and the Claude Code agentic coding product.
ground_truth.funding_ownership: Private, VC-backed. Raised a $65B Series H in May 2026 (largest private VC round in history) led by Altimeter Capital, Dragoneer, Greenoaks, and Sequoia Capital, at a $965B post-money valuation. Confidentially filed for IPO on June 1, 2026, targeting an October 2026 Nasdaq listing.
ground_truth.recent_news: Valuation roughly tripled from $380B (Feb 2026) to $965B (May 2026) in three months. Annualized revenue run rate hit $47B in May 2026, up from about $1B in Dec 2024. Claude Code reached $2.5B annualized revenue by Feb 2026.
ground_truth.risks: Extremely high revenue multiple priced for sustained hypergrowth; heavy dependence on continued enterprise adoption; intense competitive pressure from OpenAI and Google; regulatory and AI-safety scrutiny typical of frontier labs.

ground_truth.what_it_does: Creator of ChatGPT and the GPT model family; positions itself as core AI infrastructure via consumer apps, developer APIs, and the Codex coding product.
ground_truth.funding_ownership: Private, capped-profit structure under nonprofit oversight. Closed a $122B round at an $852B post-money valuation in March 2026, led by SoftBank with Amazon, Nvidia, and Microsoft as major strategic investors. Confidentially filed a draft S-1 with the SEC in June 2026.
ground_truth.recent_news: Valuation rose from $500B (Oct 2025 tender offer) to $852B (Mar 2026). Restructured its Microsoft partnership in April 2026 (non-exclusive IP license, can now serve non-Azure clouds, Microsoft revenue-share capped at $38B through 2030). As of July 2026, in preliminary talks about giving the US government an equity stake.
ground_truth.risks: Steep operating losses (loses more than $1 for every $1 of revenue per reported figures); large multi-year compute and infrastructure commitments; profitability not projected until 2030-2031 under most analyst scenarios.

ground_truth.what_it_does: Payments infrastructure company providing APIs and tools for online and in-person payment acceptance, billing, and financial operations for businesses of all sizes.
ground_truth.funding_ownership: Private, founder-led (Patrick and John Collison). Valued at roughly $159B in a February 2026 employee tender offer, up from about $91.5B a year earlier. No imminent IPO confirmed by leadership as of mid-2026.
ground_truth.recent_news: Bloomberg reported in late February 2026 that Stripe was in preliminary talks about acquiring some or all of PayPal; discussions described as early-stage and may not result in a transaction. Processed $1.9 trillion in total payment volume in 2025.
ground_truth.competitors: PayPal, Adyen, Block (Square), Shopify Payments, Affirm.
ground_truth.risks: A potential PayPal acquisition remains unconfirmed and could fall through; competitive pressure from Adyen in enterprise payments; broader fintech valuation volatility.

ground_truth.what_it_does: AI-powered workspace combining docs, wikis, databases, and project management, increasingly positioned as a platform for building AI agents and automations.
ground_truth.funding_ownership: Private. Valued at roughly $11B following a January 2026 employee tender offer (investors include Sequoia Capital, Index Ventures, GIC), versus a $10B mark from its 2021 Series C.
ground_truth.recent_news: Opened a developer platform in beta (May 2026) for building AI agents on Notion. Added native integration with Claude Code, Cursor, and Codex as AI agents (May 2026). Crossed roughly $500-600M ARR.
ground_truth.competitors: Microsoft Loop, Confluence (Atlassian), Coda, Monday.com, Asana, Google Docs.
ground_truth.risks: Microsoft Loop's deep Teams/Outlook/Office 365 integration is a structural distribution threat; largely flat headline valuation since 2021 despite revenue growth; secondary share prices reportedly declined over the prior 12 months.

ground_truth.what_it_does: Collaborative interface design and prototyping platform, spanning design, whiteboarding (FigJam), design-to-code (Dev Mode), and AI-assisted design tools.
ground_truth.funding_ownership: Public company (NYSE: FIG). IPO'd July 31, 2025 at $33/share (~$19.3B implied valuation) after Adobe's ~$20B acquisition was terminated by regulators in December 2023.
ground_truth.recent_news: Stock fell roughly 44-52% in H1 2026 despite strong Q1 2026 earnings (revenue up 46% YoY), driven by investor fears of AI-native design competitors such as Anthropic's Claude Design.
ground_truth.competitors: Adobe (Creative Cloud/XD), Canva, Sketch, Anthropic's Claude Design, Lucid.
ground_truth.risks: Market pricing in AI-native design tools as an existential threat despite strong fundamentals; still GAAP-unprofitable; high stock-based compensation.

ground_truth.what_it_does: Unified data and AI analytics platform (the "lakehouse") for data engineering, warehousing, governance, and building AI applications on enterprise data.
ground_truth.funding_ownership: Private. Confirmed $134B valuation from a Series L round closed December 2025; reportedly in talks (June 2026) to raise a new round at $165-175B, not yet closed as of mid-2026.
ground_truth.recent_news: Annualized revenue run rate of about $5.4B as of January 2026, growing over 65% YoY. CEO Ali Ghodsi indicated an IPO is more likely in 2027 than 2026.
ground_truth.competitors: Snowflake, AWS, Microsoft Azure, Google Cloud.
ground_truth.risks: Valued at more than double its closest public comparable (Snowflake) while still private; competition from cloud hyperscalers building competing native AI/data services; leadership-transition risk while preparing for a public listing.

ground_truth.what_it_does: Publicly traded AI Data Cloud platform for data warehousing, engineering, and analytics, increasingly layering in AI agent and governance tooling (e.g. Cortex AI Gateway).
ground_truth.funding_ownership: Public company (NYSE: SNOW). Market capitalization roughly $78-82B as of mid-2026.
ground_truth.recent_news: Introduced Cortex AI Gateway and additional AI security tooling in July 2026. Stock had fallen roughly 48% from its 52-week high amid AI-native competition concerns.
ground_truth.competitors: Databricks, AWS, Microsoft Azure, Google Cloud, Oracle.
ground_truth.risks: Ongoing consolidated securities class-action lawsuits over historical performance disclosures; customer-side security misconfiguration and breach exposure; consumption-based revenue model that amplifies spending-cycle swings; still GAAP-unprofitable.

ground_truth.what_it_does: Cloud-based visual design platform spanning presentations, documents, video, websites, and AI-assisted design tools ("Magic Studio"), for individuals and enterprises.
ground_truth.funding_ownership: Private, co-founder led (Melanie Perkins). Valued around $42B in an August 2025 employee share sale (up from $32B in October 2024); a major backer has said Canva is "ready" for a potential H2 2026 IPO, though no S-1 has been filed.
ground_truth.recent_news: Confirmed roughly $4B in annualized recurring revenue and 265 million monthly active users by February 2026. Profitable for eight consecutive years as of 2025.
ground_truth.competitors: Adobe (Creative Cloud/Express), Figma, Microsoft Designer, Wix, Shutterstock.
ground_truth.risks: Intensifying competition from Adobe, Figma, and Microsoft in AI-assisted design; a 2026 Australian regulatory infringement notice (~A$792,000) over late account filings, notable given IPO-readiness expectations around governance.

ground_truth.what_it_does: Chat and community platform (voice, video, text) originally built for gamers, now used broadly by online communities, creators, and developer ecosystems.
ground_truth.funding_ownership: Private. Confidentially filed a draft S-1 with the SEC in January 2026 (Goldman Sachs and JPMorgan as underwriters). Valuation estimates vary widely as of mid-2026, roughly $7-8.5B on secondary markets versus a $15B mark from its 2021 round, with bull cases as high as $25B; unconfirmed pending pricing.
ground_truth.recent_news: Public S-1 not yet released as of mid-2026; no confirmed IPO date. Reportedly generated roughly $561-879M in 2025 revenue depending on source, with 200-250 million monthly active users.
ground_truth.competitors: Slack, Roblox (community/social overlap), Reddit, Snap, Twitch.
ground_truth.risks: Revenue per user significantly lags peers like Twitter, Snap, and Reddit, a key point of valuation disagreement; rejected a ~$12B Microsoft acquisition offer in 2021 and must now prove standalone public-market viability.

ground_truth.what_it_does: No-code/low-code database and workflow platform for building custom business applications; repositioned since late 2025 as an "AI-native" company with agentic products (e.g. Superagent).
ground_truth.funding_ownership: Acquired. Bending Spoons agreed to acquire Airtable for $1.28B in cash, announced August 4, 2026 - down sharply from its 2021 peak private valuation of over $11B and a roughly $4B secondary-market mark earlier in 2025.
ground_truth.recent_news: The Bending Spoons acquisition (Aug 2026) ends Airtable's run as an independent, venture-backed company; deal expected to close by year-end 2026 pending regulatory approval.
ground_truth.risks: The acquisition price reflects a roughly 80%+ valuation decline from Airtable's 2021 peak, illustrating broader correction risk for 2021-era SaaS unicorns; integration risk under new ownership.

ground_truth.what_it_does: Frontend cloud platform for building, deploying, and scaling web applications; maintains the Next.js React framework and offers AI-native developer tools (v0, AI Cloud).
ground_truth.funding_ownership: Private. Raised a $300M Series F in September 2025 at a $9.3B post-money valuation, co-led by Accel and GIC - roughly a 3x step-up from its $3.25B valuation in May 2024.
ground_truth.recent_news: Acquired Stakpak (AI infrastructure startup) in July 2026. Revenue run rate reached roughly $340M by March 2026, growing about 84% YoY, with AI coding agents driving over 30% of weekly deployments.
ground_truth.competitors: Netlify, Cloudflare, AWS, Microsoft Azure, GitLab.
ground_truth.risks: Its v0 AI coding product faces commoditization pressure from GitHub Copilot, Cursor, Bolt.new, and similar tools; rapid AI token/inference consumption creates challenging unit economics.

ground_truth.what_it_does: Issue-tracking and project management tool purpose-built for software development teams, positioned as a faster, more opinionated alternative to Jira.
ground_truth.funding_ownership: Private. Raised an $82M Series C in June 2025 at a $1.25B valuation, led by Accel with Sequoia, 01 Advisors, and others participating.
ground_truth.recent_news: No new priced funding round confirmed since June 2025. Reported 15,000+ customers including OpenAI, Scale AI, and Perplexity, with profits reportedly up 280% year-over-year at the time of its last raise.
ground_truth.risks: Operates in a crowded project-management category dominated by much larger incumbents (Atlassian); must keep differentiating against AI features being added broadly by competitors.

ground_truth.what_it_does: Corporate spend management platform offering corporate cards, expense management, bill pay, and procurement/accounting automation.
ground_truth.funding_ownership: Private, co-founder led (Eric Glyman, Karim Atiyeh). Raised $750M in June 2026 at a $44B valuation (led by ICONIQ, GIC, and Ontario Teachers' Pension Plan) - up from $32B in November 2025 and $22.5B in July 2025.
ground_truth.recent_news: Valuation nearly tripled over roughly one year through mid-2026. Surpassed $1B in annualized recurring revenue. Growth partly attributed to companies seeking tools to manage rising AI-related spend.
ground_truth.competitors: Brex (acquired by Capital One in 2026 for $5.15B), American Express, Bill.com, Intuit (QuickBooks), Rippling.
ground_truth.risks: Meaningful revenue exposure to card interchange economics; valuation has risen extremely fast (nearly 3x in a year), raising sustainability questions if growth decelerates.

ground_truth.what_it_does: Low-code platform for building and deploying internal business software and admin tools, used by companies including Amazon, Stripe, and DoorDash.
ground_truth.funding_ownership: Private, founder-led (David Hsu). Last priced round was a $45M Series C2 in July 2022 at a $3.2B valuation; no newer priced round confirmed as of mid-2026.
ground_truth.recent_news: No major funding or M&A news identified in the past 12 months; valuation and funding figures remain those from the 2022 round.
ground_truth.competitors: Airtable, Appsmith, Bubble, Metabase, custom in-house tooling.
ground_truth.risks: Valuation stale relative to faster-moving AI-native competitors; low-code category increasingly contested by AI coding assistants that can generate internal tools directly.

ground_truth.what_it_does: AI-powered "answer engine" that synthesizes cited, sourced answers from real-time web data, plus an expanding agentic product suite (Comet browser, Perplexity Computer, an API platform).
ground_truth.funding_ownership: Private, founder-led (Aravind Srinivas). Valued at roughly $22.6B following a January 2026 Series E-6 round (investors include IVP, Accel, NEA; backers also reportedly include Jeff Bezos and Nvidia).
ground_truth.recent_news: Integrated its "Computer" agent product directly into Microsoft 365 (Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook, Teams) in June 2026. Global web traffic share reported at roughly 1.3% as of May 2026, down from 2.0% in March 2026, despite rapid ARR growth (reportedly $450-500M+ annualized).
ground_truth.competitors: Google (Search/Gemini/AI Overviews), OpenAI (ChatGPT search), Microsoft Copilot, You.com.
ground_truth.risks: Trades at a very high revenue multiple that assumes continued triple-digit growth; faces active publisher disputes (News Corp, NYT, WIRED) over content licensing/scraping; competes against far better-resourced incumbents with vastly greater distribution.
